absent: Numeric encodings of memory-policy modes, policy flags, migration flags, protection-change flags and error codes.
Full layouts of policy, weighted interleave state, access coordinates, virtual area, address space, folio and page-table entry types.
Definition and valid range of the interleave scaling factor and the distance, bandwidth and zone helpers.
Initial contents, allocation lifetime and concurrency rules for the global bandwidth table beyond the shown mutex and RCU usage.
Contracts of huge-page helpers for splitting, protection updates, migration support and shared-table detection.
Event-counter and memory-cgroup accounting semantics for NUMA protection updates.
Behavior of memory-node iteration helpers over empty or offline node sets.

findings.text: Provides nearest-node lookup over nodes in a given state, validating the state identifier and returning the input unchanged when it already satisfies the state or denotes no node, otherwise selecting the candidate with smallest distance.
Provides nearest-node lookup constrained to an explicit node mask, scanning masked candidates and returning the one with smallest distance from the origin.
Releases one reference on a memory policy object and defers reclamation through RCU when the final reference drops, permitting access from speculative mapping-lock readers.
Reports whether the mappings in a virtual area may participate in page migration, excluding device-like, DAX, unsupported huge-page and low-zone file configurations.

Updates stored per-node bandwidth from access coordinates and refreshes weighted interleave weights, preserving manual tables while keeping bandwidth current and publishing a new automatic table under lock with deferred freeing of the predecessor.
Rebinds the memory policy attached to a task against a revised allowed-node set through the shared policy rebind path.
Rebinds every virtual-area policy in an address space against a revised allowed-node set while holding the address-space write lock and marking each area for writing.
Applies NUMA protection changes over an address interval within a virtual area, gathering translation updates, counting updated pages in VM and memory-cgroup statistics, then completing the gather.

Changes page protections over an interval with caller-selected semantics for NUMA, userfault write protection and related modes, rejecting incompatible write-protection combinations and directing huge-page areas to a dedicated path.

Interleave weight reduction derives whole-number weights proportional to each memory node share of total bandwidth with a floor of one, avoiding wide division when possible, then normalizes all weights by their greatest common divisor so ratios use smallest integers.

Node performance update uses the smaller of reported read and write bandwidths, fails cleanly on allocation shortage, copies the prior bandwidth table before installing the new value, and leaves manual-mode weight tables untouched while still recording bandwidth for future automatic use.
Policy creation from a node mask rejects an empty mask, with the plain form storing the mask unchanged and the preferred form clearing the policy mask and retaining only the first set node.

Policy rebinding leaves absent policies and local-mode policies unchanged, skips work when no user mask is stored and the cpuset allowance is already equal, otherwise delegates to the handler registered for the current mode.

Nodemask rebinding honors static pinning by intersecting user and new masks and honors relative positioning through translation, otherwise remaps the active mask between old and new cpuset allowances and records the new allowance, falling back to the full new mask when the result is empty.
Default rebinding is a no-operation while preferred rebinding only records the revised cpuset allowance without altering the active node choice.

The per-mode operation table assigns nodemask creation to interleave, bind, preferred-many and weighted interleave, preferred creation to preferred only, nodemask rebinding to interleave, bind and weighted interleave, preferred rebinding to preferred and preferred-many, and no-operation rebinding to default and local.
Strict immobility holds only when strict checking is requested without either move request, in which case collection stops at the first unmovable page and reports an input-output failure.

Page collection selects folios whose node membership matches the requested mask, inverted when the invert request is set, and skips huge zero pages, absent mappings, zone-device, reserved and otherwise non-normal folios.

Large folio accounting records the most recently encountered large folio so repeated mappings of the same folio in one scan are not double counted, and a folio that cannot be isolated at its first mapping receives no retry at later mappings in the same pass.

Migration queuing avoids shared folios unless migration of all mappings is requested, isolates eligible folios from the reclaim lists before linking them for migration and updates isolated-page statistics, treating isolation failure as a refusal; an alternate build always refuses.

Huge-page collection under the huge-table lock counts migration entries as failures, requires a migratable area and an explicit move request, and additionally avoids folios shared through the page tables unless migration of all mappings is requested.

Protection updates populate missing intermediate table levels on demand and fail the walk on allocation shortage, skip absent or invalid entries, split huge block mappings when the range is partial or per-page markers are needed, and propagate per-page handling after a split.

External invalidation notification for protection changes is initialized lazily on first populated entry and closed only if it was opened, while translation-table batching brackets each virtual area and huge-page updates are tallied separately with periodic rescheduling.
Splitting for protection changes is required when write-protection tracking that relies on page-level markers is requested on a non-anonymous area.

Bandwidth-table replacement and interleave-state publication are serialized by a dedicated mutex, with the prior state read under that mutex and reclamation deferred until after unlock and an RCU grace period.
Address-space-wide rebinding holds the mapping write lock across the area scan and marks each area writable before rebinding its policy.

Page-table scans for migration hold the huge-page lock or the page-table lock while examining entries and release before continuing, with huge-page scans using the huge-table lock and periodic rescheduling on long ranges.
Policy objects are freed via RCU rather than immediately so readers under speculative mapping-lock sections remain safe even though normal accesses are serialized by the mapping lock.
Policy operation vector pairs an optional creation handler that validates and stores a node mask with a rebinding handler that adjusts a policy to a new allowance.
Migration-target context couples a policy reference with a running interleave position used to select destination nodes during allocation for migration.

Page-collection context carries a destination list, control flags, target node mask pointer, scan bounds, first area pointer, most recent large folio for deduplication, and a count of pages that could not be isolated.

Weighted interleave state moves among absent implying automatic, automatic with recomputed weights, and manual with frozen weights; bandwidth reports always advance stored bandwidth, while weight recomputation and publication occur only in automatic or absent states.

Protection range walk proceeds level by level from top-level directory to page entries, with per-level outcomes of skip absent, split and retry partial huge blocks, handle whole huge blocks, or descend, aborting the whole walk with an error on allocation failure.
Immediate freeing of policy objects would race speculative mapping-lock readers whose critical sections extend beyond normal lock boundaries; RCU deferral is required for safety.

Partial huge-block protection updates without splitting would apply page-granular semantics at block granularity; the walk must split first and retry, including clearing and repopulating file-backed entries that vanish on split.
Miscombined userfault write-protection requests within one protection change indicate caller error, producing a one-time warning and a no-operation zero result rather than applying a mixed update.
A protection range with start at or beyond end violates the walk precondition and triggers a bug check; callers must supply a non-empty ordered interval.
Policy mode identifiers distinguish default, interleave, preferred, bind, local, preferred-many and weighted interleave, bounded by a maximum mode value.
Policy flag and migration control identifiers select static versus relative node handling and strict, move, move-all and invert collection behaviors.
Protection-change control identifiers select NUMA protection, userfault write-protection set, clear and resolve variants, with architecture-gated behavior for protection-none emulation.
Node-space identifiers include memory-state selector, no-node sentinel, node-state count bound and maximum node count used for scan initialization and validation.
